description:
## Why

PKIX-ng0x decomposition, child 3 of 5. The AC has its own validity
window (separate from the issuing AA cert) and is signed by an
Attribute Authority whose own X.509 cert chain must validate against
an AA-specific trust set.

## What

1. **Validity check** (RFC 5755 §4.2.4): `AttCertValidityPeriod` is
   two `GeneralizedTime` fields. Verify `notBeforeTime <= now <=
   notAfterTime` where `now` is supplied by the caller (consistent
   with pkix-path style — no implicit SystemTime).
2. **AA chain validation** (RFC 5755 §5): the AC.signature is verified
   by the AA cert. The AA cert is itself an X.509 PKC and its chain
   must validate via `pkix_path::validate_path`. Caller supplies the
   AA cert (or a candidate AA cert pool plus AA trust anchors).
3. Composition: `validate_attribute_cert(ac, holder_pkc, aa_chain,
   aa_anchors, &policy, &verifier)` walks:
   - parse `ac` (PKIX-ng0x.1)
   - bind to `holder_pkc` (PKIX-ng0x.2)
   - check `ac.validity` against `policy.now()`
   - call `pkix_path::validate_path(aa_chain, aa_anchors, ...)` to
     validate the AA chain
   - verify `ac.signature` against `aa_chain[0]`s SPKI using the
     supplied `verifier`
   - return Ok(parsed_ac) on success, structured AcError on failure

## Tests

- [ ] Validity period: notBefore-in-future, notAfter-in-past, and
      within-window cases all map to correct verdicts.
- [ ] AA chain validation: invalid AA chain (expired, untrusted)
      causes structured failure.
- [ ] Signature failure: tampered AC.signature byte causes specific
      AcError variant, not a generic "validation failed".
- [ ] Composition: cross-check that the AA chain validation goes
      through pkix-path (does not re-implement chain walking).

## Depends on

PKIX-ng0x.1 (parser) and PKIX-ng0x.2 (binding).
title: pkix-ac: AttCertValidityPeriod + AA chain validation
